title: Agent operating settings
description: Version-controlled operating settings read from <target>/.agents/settings.json. The file is shared by every agent working on the target repository, each under its own top-level section (FR-050): this service validates the `reviewService` section strictly and ignores sibling sections belonging to other agents. Within that section, a missing or invalid REQUIRED setting stops the run (FR-028) and an unrecognized key stops the run (FR-050), while a missing OPTIONAL setting is filled from the documented `default` here and its effective value is reported with the run (FR-054). The `host` section is the exception that proves the rule: it belongs to no single agent, so it cannot sit inside one's namespace, and this service validates it as strictly as its own (research.md R-019).

hostSettings.title: Shared host settings
hostSettings.description: Settings belonging to the machine rather than to any one agent. Every agent on the host reads this section and validates it strictly; none of them owns it. Principle VIII's concurrency cap is the first such setting: it is global across every in-flight feature and task combined, and it counts any CI or reviewer job on the same host, so a cap held inside one agent's namespace — or inside one process's memory — could never satisfy it (research.md R-019).

maxConcurrentAgents.description: Maximum agent jobs running concurrently on this host, enforced by a filesystem lease under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agents/slots/ that every agent acquires before starting work and releases when it stops. Required.

reviewServiceSettings.title: Independent review service settings
reviewServiceSettings.description: This service's own section. Validated strictly: `additionalProperties: false` makes an unrecognized key an error that stops the run, because a silently ignored typo in a budget or a threshold is indistinguishable from a setting that was never applied (FR-050).
reviewServiceSettings.$comment: Cross-field invariants are not expressible in JSON Schema and are enforced in code immediately after schema validation, with the same stop-the-run consequence: reviewerTokenReserve < tokenBudget; platformApiReserve < platformApiBudget; maxReviewableDiffSize > maxPullRequestSize (otherwise FR-043 could never fire); and maxConcurrentReviews <= host.maxConcurrentAgents (R-019 — the reviewer's share can never exceed the host's cap).

requiredReviewerRoles.description: Roles whose approving verdict the merge gate requires (FR-021). Required.

blockingSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest severity that blocks merge (FR-013). Required.

maxReviewRounds.description: Maximum review rounds per pull request before the service stops and escalates (FR-020). Required.

maxReviewableDiffSize.description: Changed lines past which no review is attempted: the gate fails before any spend and the pull request must be split (FR-037). Required. Must exceed maxPullRequestSize.

maxPullRequestSize.description: Principle X discipline cap in changed lines, measured over the diff with excludedPathPatterns and git-reported binary files removed. Exceeding it is a blocking finding that a stated justification in the pull request description clears (FR-043). Required.

excludedPathPatterns.description: Declared list of path patterns excluded from line-anchored findings and from the changed-line count (FR-053). This list is the ONLY configurable source of exclusions; the service additionally excludes whatever the version control system reports as binary, and MUST NOT infer exclusions from a generated-file heuristic. Build output is kept out of the repository by .gitignore and never reaches a diff. Required — an empty array is a valid, explicit declaration that nothing is excluded by path.

tokenBudget.description: Cumulative model-token total for this repository across every pull request, every review, and every agent (FR-031, FR-047). Required.

reviewerTokenReserve.description: Share of tokenBudget drawable by review work alone, so other agents' spend cannot leave a pull request ungated (FR-047). Required. Must be less than tokenBudget.

platformApiBudget.description: Content-creating platform requests per hour the service may consume. GitHub's secondary limit is 500/hour and 80/minute; set this at or below the former. Required.

platformApiReserve.description: Remaining-request threshold at which the service stops issuing calls, notifies a human, and waits for the documented reset (FR-040). Required. Must be less than platformApiBudget.

maxRateLimitWaitSeconds.description: Longest the service may wait for a rate-limit reset before failing the gate and escalating (FR-040). Required.

maxQueueWaitSeconds.description: Longest a review may wait for a host concurrency slot before failing the gate and escalating (FR-041). Below this, the gate stays unreported. Required.

escalationChannel.description: Transport for escalation notifications. The reason is additionally stated on the pull request in every case; this channel is never substituted for that (FR-035). Required.

assignee.description: GitHub login of the human the escalation is assigned to.

label.description: Optional. Filled from the default when absent.

pollIntervalSeconds.description: How often the daemon reconciles open pull requests against the gate check runs already reported on them (research.md R-017). The listing is a conditional request, so an unchanged one costs no rate limit; this is the latency floor on noticing a push, not a cost knob. Required.

maxConcurrentReviews.description: Ceiling on the reviewer's SHARE of the host-wide agent cap (R-019). A review must hold both one of these worker slots and a host lease to start, so this can only ever reduce concurrency below host.maxConcurrentAgents, never raise it. Required. Must not exceed host.maxConcurrentAgents.

modelTransport.description: OPTIONAL (FR-054) — how the reviewer reaches the model. "api" calls the Messages API with a credential this process holds, metered against an organisation's API credits. "agent-sdk" runs Claude Code as a library, which authenticates itself and bills the operator's subscription; it constrains the response by instruction rather than by schema, so the parser is the only thing enforcing the contract. Absent, the documented default below is applied rather than stopping the run.

modelEffort.description: OPTIONAL (FR-054) — depth/cost trade-off passed to the model boundary. Absent, the documented default below is applied rather than stopping the run, and the effective value is reported with the run so that no behavior depends on a value nobody can see.

accounts.description: OPTIONAL (FR-081) — funding sources, keyed by name. An account is the thing that gets billed or throttled, and therefore the thing a budget can bound: one account may serve several providers, and when it does they draw on one metered resource. Absent, the migration synthesises a single account from `tokenBudget`/`reviewerTokenReserve` (SC-005). NOTE: in this release accounts are declared and validated but the ledger still enforces the flat `tokenBudget`/`reviewerTokenReserve`; the ledger moves onto these limits in the following pull request, at which point the flat pair is superseded.

reserve.description: `review` remains the only actor permitted to draw into it. Must be less than this account's budget — enforced in code, like every other cross-field invariant here.

providers.description: OPTIONAL (FR-076, FR-077) — named ways of reaching one model family each, keyed by name. Absent, the migration synthesises a single provider from `modelTransport`. MUST NOT be declared alongside `modelTransport`: two descriptions of how a model is reached is one more than can be true.

routes.description: OPTIONAL (FR-076) — the ordered provider list each reviewer role is asked in, keyed by role. Advanced only on a capacity failure (FR-078), exhausted rather than restarted (FR-080). Absent, the migration gives every required role a single-entry route.

authoringProvider.description: OPTIONAL (FR-082) — the provider the authoring identity uses. Named explicitly rather than inferred: an independence rule that infers who the author was cannot be validated at preflight, and one that is not validated at preflight is discovered after the spend. It carries its own `family` rather than referencing an entry in `providers`, because the author is not a reviewer provider — it has no route, no credential this service resolves and no containment this service enforces, and demanding a full provider declaration for something never invoked would be a fiction. No required reviewer role may run on a provider whose `family` matches this one, unless `authoringProviderOverrideReason` is present.

authoringProviderOverrideReason.description: OPTIONAL (FR-082) — a recorded, version-controlled reason permitting a required reviewer role to run on the authoring provider's model family. Its presence is the override; there is no boolean, because an override without a stated reason is the thing Principle VI forbids.

route.title: One reviewer role's ordered provider list
route.description: Non-empty, no provider twice, every name declared in `providers`, and short enough that its attempts at the FR-086 bound cannot outlast `maxQueueWaitSeconds` — all enforced in code after schema validation.

provider.title: One named way of reaching one model family
provider.description: Distinct from a *transport*, which is how the family is reached. FR-083: a provider MUST NOT be addable without stating how it satisfies each containment obligation, because reviewed content is untrusted data whichever vendor reads it.

models.description: The exact model identifier per effort level. Required and never defaulted (R-021): a vendor default can change between releases, and a family nobody pinned is a family the FR-082 check never saw. Effort is expressed HERE rather than by a separate flag, so a provider serves only the effort levels it pins a model for; a configured `modelEffort` with no entry is a preflight failure, not a silent downgrade (FR-060).

family.description: The model family every entry in `models` resolves to. The FR-082 independence check compares families, never vendor labels — an aggregator can serve the authoring family under another vendor's name (R-021).

transport.description: How the family is reached. `cli` spawns a vendor binary and parses its JSON output, discharging containment at the spawn rather than in the dependency tree.

funding.description: Recorded so Principle IV's no-new-metered-spend assumption is checkable rather than asserted.

account.description: Which declared account this provider draws on. Two providers sharing one account are independent in judgement and NOT in capacity (R-029); such a pair does not satisfy SC-001.

credential.description: What preflight must find before any spend (FR-084). An `oauth-profile` legitimately carries no key; only a source that promises a key and then supplies an empty one is rejected.

name.description: The variable, keychain item or path the credential is read from, where the source needs one.

containment.description: FR-083. Every obligation must be stated; a declaration missing any is a schema error, not a warning. These are assertions the provider implementation is required to honour at the call site, and preflight checks that the operator declared them.

vendorSandbox.description: OPTIONAL — a restriction the vendor itself enforces, where one exists. Structural rather than a matter of our own compliance (Principle V), so it is recorded when available.

hostSurfaces.description: OPTIONAL — host surfaces the child opens that are not egress, declared rather than discovered (R-028): a loopback listener, local state written. Naming them is the obligation; they are not prohibited.
